meaning.en: To accept criticism and advice readily and without resistance.
meaning.zh: 乐于接受别人的批评和劝告，像流水一样顺畅。

examples.zh: 好领导应当从谏如流，才能少犯错误。
examples.en: A good leader should take advice readily so as to make fewer mistakes.

examples.zh: 公司对客户的意见从谏如流，产品改进很快。
examples.en: The company acts on customer feedback at once, so its products improve quickly.

usage.en: Praises a ruler, leader or boss. Often paired with 虚心纳谏. The form 纳谏如流 is also used.
usage.zh: 赞扬君主、领导善于接受意见。常与“虚心纳谏”连用。也作“纳谏如流”。

meaning.en: A rich, fertile region with plentiful resources, especially the Sichuan Basin.
meaning.zh: 物产丰富、土地肥沃的地方，特指四川。

examples.zh: 四川自古被称为天府之国。
examples.en: Sichuan has been known since ancient times as the land of plenty.

examples.zh: 这片平原水土丰美，真是天府之国。
examples.en: This plain has rich soil and water; it is truly a land of abundance.

story.en: In the Warring States Strategies, the strategist Su Qin describes the Qin heartland, with Ba and Shu, as a 'heavenly storehouse' (天府). The phrase later came to mean Sichuan.
story.zh: 《战国策·秦策一》中苏秦称秦国地势富饶，为“天府”。后来专指四川。

usage.en: Nearly always a noun; strongly associated with Sichuan (the Chengdu Plain).
usage.zh: 作名词；常特指四川成都平原。

meaning.en: To repay a kindness with harm or ill will.
meaning.zh: 用怨恨回报别人的恩惠。

equivalents: bite the hand that feeds you

examples.zh: 他帮过你那么多次，你却以怨报德，太不应该了。
examples.en: He helped you so many times and you repaid him with spite; that was wrong.

examples.zh: 别对帮助过你的人以怨报德。
examples.en: Don't bite the hand that has helped you.

usage.en: Condemns ingratitude. Opposite of 以德报怨 (repay hatred with kindness).
usage.zh: 谴责忘恩。与“以德报怨”相反。

natural: not dare to ask about the ford

meaning.en: Not daring to enquire about or approach something, usually because it is too costly or difficult.
meaning.zh: 不敢去打听或尝试，多因太贵或太难。

examples.zh: 房价太高，许多年轻人对买房不敢问津。
examples.en: With house prices so high, many young people dare not even look at buying.

examples.zh: 这家餐厅的价格让普通顾客不敢问津。
examples.en: The prices put ordinary customers off entirely.

usage.en: Usually about expensive or risky things. Do not confuse with 无人问津 (nobody shows interest).
usage.zh: 多指价格高或风险大的事物。注意与“无人问津”区分。

meaning.en: Used when accepting an offer or gift, because refusing it would seem impolite.
meaning.zh: 推辞别人的好意显得不恭敬，所以接受。

equivalents: it would be rude to refuse

examples.zh: 既然你这么热情，我就却之不恭了。
examples.en: Since you are so kind, it would be rude to refuse.

examples.zh: 这份礼物却之不恭，受之有愧。
examples.en: It would be rude to decline this gift, yet I feel unworthy of it.

story.en: Mencius says that when a gift is offered, repeatedly refusing it is disrespectful (却之却之为不恭).

usage.en: Polite formula. Often followed by 受之有愧 (accepting it makes me feel unworthy).
usage.zh: 客套话，常与“受之有愧”连用。

meaning.en: Prevented from acting by circumstances and conditions.
meaning.zh: 受到客观形势的阻碍和限制，不能行动。

examples.zh: 当时形格势禁，他无法公开表态。
examples.en: Circumstances were restrictive then, so he could not state his position openly.

examples.zh: 由于形格势禁，计划只好暂停。
examples.en: Because conditions blocked us, the plan had to be suspended.

story.en: Sun Bin advised helping Zhao by striking Wei's rear: 'when the situation hinders and restricts, the difficulty resolves itself' (形格势禁，则自为解耳).
story.zh: 孙膑对田忌说：“批亢捣虚，形格势禁，则自为解耳。”

usage.en: Formal, written. 格 means 'obstruct'. Often misread as 'shape'.
usage.zh: 书面语。“格”是阻碍的意思。

meaning.en: Gentle, sincere and generous in character; also used of poetry that is mild and restrained.
meaning.zh: 性情温和善良、诚恳宽厚；也指诗文委婉含蓄。

examples.zh: 她温柔敦厚，从不与人争吵。
examples.en: She is gentle and generous and never quarrels with anyone.

examples.zh: 他的诗风温柔敦厚，读来如沐春风。
examples.en: His poetry is mild and restrained, pleasant as a spring breeze.

story.en: The Book of Rites says the teaching of the Odes makes people 'gentle, kind and sincere' (温柔敦厚，《诗》教也).

usage.en: Praise for people or literary style. Pronounce 敦 as dūn.
usage.zh: 褒义，形容人或诗风。“敦”读dūn。

meaning.en: Time passes on like flowing water and never returns.
meaning.zh: 时间像流水一样不停流逝，一去不返。

equivalents: time flows on like a river

examples.zh: 看着老照片，才惊觉逝者如斯，转眼二十年过去了。
examples.en: Looking at the old photos, I realised time flows on; twenty years had passed in a blink.

examples.zh: 逝者如斯，珍惜当下吧。
examples.en: Time passes like running water; cherish the present.

story.en: Standing by a river, Confucius said: 'What passes is like this, never stopping day or night.'
story.zh: 孔子在河边感叹：“逝者如斯夫！不舍昼夜。”

usage.en: Literary sigh about time. Often with 不舍昼夜.
usage.zh: 文学性感叹，常与“不舍昼夜”连用。

pinyin: jiāng shān yì gǎi, běn xìng nán yí
literal: rivers · mountains · easy · change · nature · hard · move
natural: rivers and mountains may change, nature cannot

meaning.en: A person's basic nature is very hard to change.
meaning.zh: 一个人的本性很难改变。

equivalents: a leopard cannot change its spots
a tiger cannot change its stripes

examples.zh: 他赌瘾又犯了，真是江山易改，本性难移。
examples.en: His gambling habit is back; a leopard cannot change its spots.

examples.zh: 都说江山易改，本性难移，你就别指望他改了。
examples.en: As they say, you can't change a person's nature; don't count on him changing.

usage.en: Usually said of bad habits. Often used as a full proverb; the first half alone is rare.
usage.zh: 多指坏习惯。常说全句。

synonyms: 狗改不了吃屎——本性难移

natural: dress before dawn, eat after dark

meaning.en: To work extremely hard from early morning until late at night, said especially of a ruler or official.
meaning.zh: 天不亮就穿衣，天黑了才吃饭，形容勤于政事。

examples.zh: 这位市长宵衣旰食，为城市建设操劳。
examples.en: The mayor works from dawn till dusk on the city's development.

examples.zh: 科研人员宵衣旰食，终于攻克难关。
examples.en: The researchers worked tirelessly and finally broke through.

usage.en: Praises diligent leaders. 旰 is read gàn. Formal.
usage.zh: 赞扬勤政。“旰”读gàn。书面语。

natural: death would not atone for it

meaning.en: Even death is not enough punishment for the crimes committed.
meaning.zh: 犯下的罪行极重，就是处死也抵偿不了。

equivalents: deserve to die many times over

examples.zh: 这些贩毒集团的头目死有余辜。
examples.en: The heads of that drug ring deserve far worse than death.

examples.zh: 他害了那么多人，真是死有余辜。
examples.en: He harmed so many people; he truly deserves what he gets.

usage.en: Strong condemnation; use carefully. 辜 means 'crime'.
usage.zh: 语气很重。“辜”指罪过。

meaning.en: An improper wish or ambition beyond what one is entitled to.
meaning.zh: 不符合自己身份、本分的想法或欲望。

examples.zh: 他对公司的财产起了非分之想。
examples.en: He began to covet the company's property.

examples.zh: 我对这个职位绝无非分之想。
examples.en: I have no improper designs on this position at all.

usage.en: Usually with 有/起/存. 分 here is read fèn. Often in denials: 绝无非分之想.
usage.zh: 常与“有、起、存”搭配。“分”读fèn。常用于否定表态。

natural: mislead the public with wild talk

meaning.en: To spread outrageous falsehoods and deceive the public.
meaning.zh: 用荒唐邪说迷惑群众。

equivalents: spread lies to mislead the public

examples.zh: 有人在网上妖言惑众，扰乱社会秩序。
examples.en: Some people online mislead the public with wild claims and disturb order.

examples.zh: 他靠妖言惑众骗取钱财。
examples.en: He cheats people of money by deceiving them with false doctrines.

usage.en: Accusatory; often about rumours, cults or fake health claims.
usage.zh: 带指责意味，常指谣言、邪教、伪科学。

meaning.en: To rob and plunder houses by force, as bandits do.
meaning.zh: 成群结伙闯进人家抢劫财物。

examples.zh: 土匪打家劫舍，百姓苦不堪言。
examples.en: Bandits raided and looted homes and the people suffered terribly.

examples.zh: 这伙流氓在村里打家劫舍，无恶不作。
examples.en: That gang plundered the village and committed every crime.

usage.en: Often in historical or fiction settings, about bandits.
usage.zh: 多用于历史、小说中，指土匪强盗。

natural: why worry about lacking a pretext

meaning.en: If someone wants to blame you, there is always some excuse to be found.
meaning.zh: 想要给人加罪，不愁找不到借口。

equivalents: you can always find a pretext
a stick to beat a dog

examples.zh: 他存心整你，何患无辞？
examples.en: If he is set on getting you, he will find a pretext.

examples.zh: 欲加之罪，何患无辞，你再怎么解释也没用。
examples.en: If they want to blame you they will find a reason; no explanation will help.

story.en: Duke Xian's son Li Ke was told by his enemy that he had killed the ruler; Li Ke replied 'if you want to condemn someone, you will never lack words' (欲加之罪，其无辞乎).
story.zh: 里克被逼自杀时说：“欲加之罪，其无辞乎？”

usage.en: Usually the full saying 欲加之罪，何患无辞. Complains about unfair accusations.
usage.zh: 常说“欲加之罪，何患无辞”，表达对无端指责的不满。

natural: save people from suffering and disaster

meaning.en: To rescue people from hardship and disaster, as a compassionate deity does.
meaning.zh: 解救受苦受难的人，多指菩萨的慈悲。

equivalents: come to the aid of those in distress

examples.zh: 观音菩萨被称为救苦救难的大慈大悲。
examples.en: Guanyin is called the merciful saviour who rescues from suffering.

examples.zh: 志愿者们救苦救难，赢得了人们的敬意。
examples.en: The volunteers relieved the suffering and earned people's respect.

usage.en: Often in the title 救苦救难观世音菩萨; used humorously of someone's rescuer.
usage.zh: 常见于“救苦救难观世音菩萨”，口语中也可戏称救星。

meaning.en: To impose heavy, arbitrary taxes and extort money from the people.
meaning.zh: 向人民强征苛捐杂税。

examples.zh: 地方官横征暴敛，百姓流离失所。
examples.en: The local officials levied crushing taxes and the people were left homeless.

examples.zh: 历史上横征暴敛的王朝往往很快覆灭。
examples.en: Dynasties that taxed brutally often fell quickly.

usage.en: Describes tyrannical rule. 横 here is read héng (arbitrary).
usage.zh: 指暴政。“横”读héng，意为蛮横。

natural: eat raw flesh and drink blood

meaning.en: To eat raw meat, hair and all, and drink blood, as in primitive times.
meaning.zh: 原始人不会用火，生吃禽兽，连毛带血。

examples.zh: 远古人类还过着茹毛饮血的生活。
examples.en: Ancient humans still lived on raw meat and blood.

examples.zh: 他把那些野蛮的做法形容为茹毛饮血。
examples.en: He described those savage practices as primitive.

story.en: The Book of Rites says that early people 'ate the flesh of birds and beasts and drank their blood, and wore their feathers and fur' (饮其血，茹其毛).

usage.en: Describes primitive life, or figuratively savage behaviour. 血 is read xuè here.
usage.zh: 形容原始生活，也可比喻野蛮。“血”读xuè。

meaning.en: Classical function words; mocks stilted, pedantic classical-style speech or writing.
meaning.zh: 文言虚词，讽刺说话写文章咬文嚼字、半文不白。

examples.zh: 他一开口就是之乎者也，让人听不懂。
examples.en: He starts every sentence with stilted archaic phrases nobody understands.

examples.zh: 文章少些之乎者也，读者才容易接受。
examples.en: If the writing had less archaic pedantry, readers could take it in more easily.

usage.en: Mildly mocking. Used for pretentious or old-fashioned wording.
usage.zh: 略带讽刺，指咬文嚼字。

meaning.en: Having seen the great sea, nothing smaller impresses; one who has known great love or experience finds lesser ones unmoving.
meaning.zh: 见过大海，别的水就难以称奇；比喻阅历丰富或爱情深厚后，别的都难以入眼。

equivalents: having seen the ocean, no stream will do

examples.zh: 曾经沧海难为水，他再也没有爱上别人。
examples.en: Having seen the sea, no other water will do; he never loved anyone else.

examples.zh: 他曾经沧海，对这点荣誉毫不在意。
examples.en: With all he has experienced, such an honour means little to him.

story.en: Yuan Zhen, mourning his wife, wrote: 'Having seen the great sea, other waters are nothing; beyond Mount Wu, no clouds are clouds' (曾经沧海难为水，除却巫山不是云).
story.zh: 元稹悼念亡妻：“曾经沧海难为水，除却巫山不是云。”

usage.en: Usually quoted as 曾经沧海难为水. Used for both love and broad experience. 难为水 is the second half.
usage.zh: 多用全句“曾经沧海难为水”，可指爱情或阅历。

natural: the sun is three poles high

meaning.en: The sun is high in the sky; it is late morning.
meaning.zh: 太阳已升得很高，指时间不早了。

equivalents: the sun is high in the sky

examples.zh: 都日上三竿了，你还不起床？
examples.en: The sun's high up already and you still aren't out of bed?

examples.zh: 周末他总是睡到日上三竿才起来。
examples.en: At weekends he sleeps until mid-morning.

usage.en: Typically about oversleeping. Often follows 睡到.
usage.zh: 多指睡懒觉，常说“睡到日上三竿”。

natural: to catch bandits, catch their chief

meaning.en: To solve a problem or defeat a group, deal with its leader first.
meaning.zh: 要制服敌人，先抓住它的首领；比喻抓住关键。

equivalents: cut off the head of the snake

examples.zh: 警方擒贼擒王，抓获了诈骗团伙的头目。
examples.en: The police went for the ringleader and arrested the fraud gang's boss.

examples.zh: 管理上要擒贼擒王，先解决核心问题。
examples.en: In management, tackle the key issue first.

story.en: Du Fu wrote: 'To shoot a man, shoot his horse first; to catch bandits, catch their chief first' (射人先射马，擒贼先擒王).
story.zh: 杜甫《前出塞》：“射人先射马，擒贼先擒王。”

usage.en: A strategy idiom; 擒贼先擒王 is also said.
usage.zh: 谋略成语，也说“擒贼先擒王”。

meaning.en: To try every possible means to achieve something.
meaning.zh: 想尽各种办法。

examples.zh: 他想方设法凑齐了学费。
examples.en: He found every means to raise the tuition fees.

examples.zh: 公司想方设法降低成本。
examples.en: The company is trying every means to cut costs.

usage.en: Followed by a verb phrase describing the goal. Neutral; focuses on effort.
usage.zh: 后接要达成的目标，中性，强调努力。

pinyin: jìn zhū zhě chì, jìn mò zhě hēi
literal: near · cinnabar · one · red, near · ink · one · black
natural: you take on the colour of your company

meaning.en: You become like the company you keep: good friends make you better, bad ones make you worse.
meaning.zh: 接近好人使人变好，接近坏人使人变坏，比喻环境对人影响很大。

equivalents: you become like the company you keep

examples.zh: 近朱者赤，跟优秀的人在一起你也会进步。
examples.en: You pick up good qualities from good company; being with great people will improve you.

examples.zh: 近朱者赤，他进了好班级后成绩提高了。
examples.en: Good company rubs off; his grades went up after he joined a good class.

examples.zh: 近墨者黑，你别再跟那帮人混了。
examples.en: Bad company corrupts; stop hanging out with that lot.

story.en: Fu Xuan wrote: 'Stay near cinnabar and you turn red; stay near ink and you turn black.'
story.zh: 傅玄《太子少傅箴》：“近朱者赤，近墨者黑。”

usage.en: Usually paired with 近墨者黑 as one saying. The 近朱者赤 half encourages choosing good friends.
usage.zh: 常与“近墨者黑”成对，鼓励择善而交。

synonyms: 染于苍则苍，染于黄则黄
